// Expected values for the fisher's work (docs/rules/fishing.md), captured from the original program in the emulator (ADR 0008):
// tools/GhidraDump/emulate.py, the verb goods with a finished type 1 building (the fisher's) at the flag 17,3 of a game whose map
// has a lake east of the castle, reduced to the passes that matter. A scenario starts with a "#" line that names its verb command;
// each line after it gives, for a pass, the 16 bytes of the castle's fisher (slot 15, s15=) where his node, state, timers, or
// counters changed, the 18 bytes of the building (b=) where they changed, the object bytes that changed (o=x,y:old>new;...), the lake
// details that changed (ld=x,y:old>new;...), the flag's byte 4 and goods bytes (g=) where they changed, the castle's count of fish
// (fish=) where it changed, and the generator's words (rng=) as they stand. The verb takes the dummy of the flag table, so its flag
// slots are the engine's plus one. Pass 0 has no ld= line: the verb lists the first pass's change against a map the castle's
// placement has not marked yet. A cast whose lake detail is not 0 draws against it and lowers it by one on a catch (fisher-lake,
// the pass 1730); a fisher who makes ten casts with no catch turns back with nothing (fisher-dry-lake, the pass 2076). The scenario fisher-dry-lake
// runs the same game as fisher-lake and writes a lake detail of 0 into the nodes x 20 to 30, y 0 to 12 before the pass 940 (the verb's SET
// of the form ld@PASS,X0,Y0,X1,Y1,VALUE; the rectangle holds no flag or building node, whose link takes the same byte). Its lines before
// the pass 938 list only the lake details, and the ld= line of the pass 940 is the verb's own write. His ten casts draw nothing, so the
// generator's words stay the same through them, and the detail of the node he casts at stays 0. Not production
// code: no routine of the program is transcribed here, only values the program produced.
